(This evening through Monday)...
Issued at 201 PM EDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Surface analysis early this afternoon shows southwest flow in place 
across Indiana. This was due to a weak trough of low pressure 
stretched from northern Michigan to IA and NRN KS and strong high 
pressure in place across the southeastern states. GOES19 shows 
scattered clouds were still found across central Indiana with more 
abundant cloud cover over MO and IL where light showers were 
present. Dew points were quite high, in the lower 70s. Aloft, water 
vapor shows mainly a NW flow in place. streaming from MT and WY, 
across the upper midwest, before slipping slightly south to the 
southern Great Lakes and northeastern states. A weak disturbance was 
found over IA, helping to trigger those light showers to the SE.

Tonight...Uncertainty remains high for shower and storm chances. 
Forecast soundings show deep CAPE available this evening but a CAP 
appears to remain in place within the lower levels, limiting deep 
convection. Provided the CAP holds, dry weather will be expected 
through much of the evening across and into the overnight. Some of 
the forcing to the west within the NW flow aloft should propagate 
across northern Indiana overnight. This will be our best triggering 
feature tonight. Thus will try and limit pops to the northern and 
northeast parts of the forecast area where those dynamics are more 
likely to pass. Caveat and low confidence remains for isolated 
showers or storms late this afternoon and into the evening. The warm 
and humid air mass in place will result in lows in the upper 60s and 
lower 70s.

Tuesday and Tuesday Night...

Models agree with more forcing aloft within the NW flow aloft 
passing across Central Indiana during the afternoon and evening 
hours. This forcing along with the very warm and moist airmass in 
place will be favorable for additional shower and storm development 
on Tuesday afternoon. Forecast soundings show deep CAPE across the 
area with values over 3300 J/KG. Also PWATS will be over 2 inches. 
HRRR suggests an area of thunderstorms over Central Indiana during 
peak heating hours on Tuesday afternoon and into the evening. These 
storms will have the potential to be severe with strong updrafts 
capable of producing damaging straight line winds and heavy rainfall 
resulting in flooding. Confidence on precise timing and locations 
remain low. This will use high pops over a larger window late 
tomorrow and tomorrow evening. Again, westerly flow and a warm and 
humid air in place will allow for high temperatures in the upper 80s 
to around 90.

Wednesday and Wednesday Night...

The similar NW flow aloft will remain in place across Central 
Indiana and the upper midwest on Wednesday and Wednesday Night. 
Again, models suggest yet another wave to pass across Indiana within 
this flow. Some ridging pushing easting should allow the flow to 
become a bit more NW, which would allow for storm development and 
propagation to be more impactful across all of our forecast area 
rather than just the north. Forecast soundings on Wednesday again 
suggest deep CAPE aloft, over 3500 J/KG, but a cap in place once 
again through the middle of the afternoon. This should allow us to 
include dry weather through the first parts of the day, followed 
higher pops in the mid afternoon into the evening. Again, highs 
will reach the mid to upper 80s. Once again, heavy rains will be 
possible, but high uncertainty remains.

Thursday and Friday...

The upper pattern during this time is suggested to continue as NW 
flow aloft, but evolve to ridging building across the central 
Plains. Embedded waves within the flow are suggested to pass on 
Thursday Night, with weak ridging building across IL and the western 
Great Lakes. Within the lower levels a weak, warm frontal boundary 
looks to be lingering across Central Indiana before sagging 
southward to on Friday. This with a warm, humid and unstable air 
mass in place will be sufficient to include pops, particularly on 
Thursday as the best wave and lower level trough will be in place at 
that time.  Again highs in the mid and upper 80s will be in place on 
Thursday, with slightly cooler values on Friday as winds take a more 
northeasterly component as the front sags southward.

Saturday through Monday...

Aloft, strong high pressure is suggested to set up over the lower 
Mississippi valley, with a ring of fire possible set-up impacting 
northern and Central Indiana. Several embedded short waves are 
suggested to push across Central Indiana through this time amid the 
west to northwest flow. Forecast soundings suggest a conditional 
situation, with plenty of CAPE available each day yet still a CAP 
suggested each day also. Thus overall, confidence remains low for 
showers and storms, but enough ingredients remain present to 
necessitate  at least some mention of pops. Above normal 
temperatures are expected to continue this weekend.
